content.title: Belief in God in light of tsunamis
content.speakers: William Lane Craig · A. C. Grayling
content.description: Study how natural suffering challenges belief in a good and powerful God.

claim.text: Craig distinguishes logical and probabilistic versions of the problem of evil and defends belief in God. Grayling challenges that defense and presents a secular response to suffering.

content.hinge: Does an objection claim that God and suffering are logically incompatible, or that suffering makes God’s existence unlikely?
prompts: Identify which version of the problem of evil is being discussed.
Distinguish possible reasons for suffering from known reasons.
Evaluate the practical response to suffering separately from the existence argument.
content.transcriptCoverage: Both openings, rebuttals, three question groups and closing statements. The supplied text marks a missing question summary and the beginning of Grayling's answer in the second question group, plus inaudible passages. Recording alignment has not been independently checked.

reviews.scope: Transcript source, event identity, editorial summary, coverage notes and YouTube metadata review
reviews.note: Checked linked transcript structures and publisher notices; compared participant/event descriptions with the recording listings. Verified YouTube metadata and runtimes on 2026-10-11; rejected a 9:12 Concept of God excerpt and selected the 1:31:47 debate. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. Full recordings were not watched or heard, and word-for-word alignment and whole-event completeness remain unverified. No external transcript body is republished. Existing doctrinal policy is unchanged.
